test_methodology: Deterministic negative tests. For each category, a synthetic offending package or condition is constructed and evaluated against the Core Package-Composition Gate. Expected behavior: explicit fail-closed with named failure category. Silent reconciliation would be a defect.

tests.scenario: A synthetic bolt-on 'X' declares capabilities_supplied = ['constitutional.ptr-principles-cp1-cp7'] (a Core-owned capability).
tests.expected_result: Core Package-Composition Gate fails closed with 'duplicate_capability_ownership' (capability_id already authoritatively owned by CoSyn-v16.0.0 Core cosyn-constitution-v16.0.0.md). Bolt-on rejected.
tests.verification: Traced through cosyn-v16-extension-contract-v16.0.0.md §4 step 3 (bolt-on manifest verification) and §5 duplicate_capability_ownership rule. Core capability-ownership-map.json shows single_ownership_registry entry for 'constitutional.ptr-principles-cp1-cp7' with authoritative_owner = 'CoSyn-v16.0.0 Core (cosyn-constitution-v16.0.0.md)'. No dual-ownership possible.

tests.scenario: Two synthetic bolt-ons 'A' and 'B' both declare capabilities_supplied = ['writing-personas.seven-persona-governance'].
tests.expected_result: §4 step 4 (Cross-bolt-on conflict scan) fails closed with 'duplicate_capability_ownership'. Composition halts.
tests.verification: Extension contract §4 step 4 explicitly performs cross-bolt-on scan and fails closed on dual claim. capability-ownership-map documents single ownership.

tests.scenario: A synthetic Tier-3 project package declares capabilities_supplied = ['constitutional.canonical-turn-lifecycle'] (attempts to override Core).
tests.expected_result: §4 step 6 rejects Tier-3 packages that attempt to override Core, Tier-2, or applicable bolt-on authority. Fail closed with 'tier3_authority_escalation'.
tests.verification: cosyn-constitution-v16.0.0.md §17 rule 5 explicitly prohibits Tier-3 authority escalation. Extension contract §5 lists as fail-closed category.

tests.scenario: A synthetic bolt-on declares required_core_generation = '15.0.2'. Loaded against Core v16.0.0.
tests.expected_result: §5 version_incompatibility fires. Fail closed. Loading rejected.
tests.verification: Extension contract §5 explicitly enumerates version_incompatibility. Core bind template pins required_core_generation = '16.0.0'; mismatch triggers halt.

tests.scenario: A synthetic bolt-on declares dependencies = ['some-other-bolt-on-v16.0.0'] which is not present in the composition.
tests.expected_result: §5 missing_dependency fires. Fail closed.
tests.verification: Extension contract §5 enumerates missing_dependency.

tests.scenario: An attempt to load PersonaGovernor_v2.5.2.md directly into a v16 composition (outside an explicitly authorized adapter package).
tests.expected_result: §5 legacy_governance_injection fires. Fail closed. cosyn-constitution-v16.0.0.md §18 declares no implicit v16 compatibility with CGS v15. Zero adapter packages are authorized in v16.0.0 (per cosyn-v16-bind-template-v16.0.0.json legacy_compatibility.adapter_packages_authorized = []).
tests.verification: Extension contract §5 legacy_governance_injection rule. Constitution §18 legacy boundary.

tests.scenario: A synthetic bolt-on's internal cross-references point to 'ptr-specification-v15.0.2.md' (different version than loaded v16.0.0).
tests.expected_result: §5 stale_version_declaration fires. Fail closed.
tests.verification: Extension contract §5 stale_version_declaration rule. Stack Architect §10 State and Version Hygiene requires version labels to match bound artifacts.

tests.scenario: Two bolt-ons extend anti-ai-signature-gate.base-detection-and-rewrite with mutually contradictory rewrite priorities and Core does not define deterministic merge behavior.
tests.expected_result: §4 step 5 (Cross-bolt-on extension scan) fires. Fail closed with 'conflicting_bolt_ons'.
tests.verification: Extension contract §4 step 5 explicitly performs cross-bolt-on extension conflict detection. §5 enumerates conflicting_bolt_ons.

tests.scenario: A synthetic bolt-on declares capabilities_extended targeting a capability that no higher layer authoritatively owns (e.g., a capability_id that is not in the capability-ownership-map).
tests.expected_result: §4 step 3 (Enumerate applicable bolt-ons — verify each capabilities_extended entry resolves to a Core-owned capability) fails closed with 'unauthorized_extension'.
tests.verification: Extension contract §3 requires core_owner_reference to be substantiated by capability-ownership-map. §5 unauthorized_extension.

tests.scenario: creative-writing-v16.0.0 loaded into a project whose declared expertise scope does NOT include creative writing (e.g., a software-engineering project).
tests.expected_result: §5 wrong_context_bolt_on_load fires. Fail closed unless the project explicitly declares the bolt-on applicable. creative-writing-v16.0.0 manifest.applicability_declaration explicitly requires 'project's declared expertise scope includes creative writing'.
tests.verification: creative-writing-package-manifest-v16.0.0.json applicability_declaration field. Extension contract §5 wrong_context_bolt_on_load. creative-writing-bind-template applicability_declaration.

tests.scenario: A synthetic future Tier-2 package declares capabilities_supplied = ['ptr.record-schema-and-lifecycle'] (a Core capability).
tests.expected_result: §4 step 2 explicitly verifies Tier-2 supplies only capabilities in the Tier-2 reserved space. Rejects Tier-2 packages supplying Core-owned capabilities. Fail closed.
tests.verification: Extension contract §4 step 2. Constitution §17 reserved binding positions defines Tier-2 reserved capability categories (user-response, user-voice-style, user-editing-preference, user-memory-context-control) — PTR schema is NOT in that set.

tests.scenario: A Tier-3 project package attempts to override a Creative Writing bolt-on rule (e.g., disable the naturalness standard for the project).
tests.expected_result: §4 step 6 rejects Tier-3 override of applicable bolt-on. Fail closed. (User MAY authorize a specific naturalness-item bypass per anti-ai-fiction-naturalness §7 Author Control Interaction — but that is explicit user override, not silent Tier-3 override.)
tests.verification: Constitution §17 rule 5. Extension contract §5 tier3_authority_escalation.

tests.scenario: A file listed in manifest_files is not present in the package, or a file is present that is not listed.
tests.expected_result: §5 manifest_actual_file_mismatch fires. Fail closed. Verified in Phase 9 Validation 6 for both Core and CW packages: 0 mismatches.
tests.verification: Phase 9 Validation 4/5/6 confirmed manifests match actual files for both packages.

tests.scenario: Any file's actual SHA-256 does not match the declared integrity_hashes entry.
tests.expected_result: §5 hash_mismatch fires. Fail closed. Verified in Phase 9 Validation 1/2: 0 mismatches for Core and CW.
tests.verification: Phase 9 Validation 1 (Core, 11 files) and Validation 2 (CW, 22 files) — all hashes match.

tests.scenario: A derived artifact lacks a provenance-pointer to its source basis.
tests.expected_result: §5 missing_provenance fires. Fail closed.
tests.verification: build/provenance/migration-provenance-map.json contains an entry for EVERY derived artifact in Core (12 files) and CW bolt-on (23 files, grouped where identical treatment applies). Each entry identifies source basis, retained content, excluded content, moved content, semantic changes, and reason. Core and CW package manifests both declare provenance_pointer field.

tests.scenario: A rule is authoritatively declared in both Core and a bolt-on (e.g., anti-ai base gate rules re-declared inside the CW bolt-on).
tests.expected_result: Fail closed by design: capability-ownership-map single_ownership_registry allows only one authoritative_owner per capability_id. Extension contract §3 prohibits restating base semantics in extensions.
tests.verification: capability-ownership-map.json enumerates 45+ capabilities each with exactly one authoritative_owner. anti-ai-fiction-naturalness-v16.0.0.md §0 explicitly declares it is an extension and MUST NOT weaken any check in Core §5/6/7/8. Writing-mode-registry-v16.0.0 explicitly binds Core Mode Registry as base authority and does not restate Core schema.

tests.scenario: A synthetic bolt-on adds a mode-registry entry containing `bypass: true`.
tests.expected_result: mode-registry-v16.0.0.md §3 declares prohibited fields (bypass/exemption/override/gate_suppression). Any such field is a registration failure. §5 requires bolt-on extension registries to omit every prohibited field. Fail closed.
tests.verification: mode-registry-v16.0.0.md §3, §5.

tests.scenario: CW bolt-on fiction PCR protocol attempts to mark a state-delta item as pcr-promoted without pcr_ratification_link.
tests.expected_result: Core PTR §20 requires pcr_ratification_link; Governor PTR Enforcement Gate blocks silent PCR promotion (Class 0 failure). Fail closed. fiction-pcr-protocol-v16.0.0 explicitly declares it does not weaken Core §20 ratification rules.
tests.verification: cosyn-constitution-v16.0.0.md §7 Class 0 list; persona-governor-v16.0.0.md §11 PCR promotion guard; ptr-specification-v16.0.0.md §20 promotion rules; capability-ownership-map boundary between Core PCR framework and CW fiction PCR.

tests.scenario: CW bolt-on fiction-recovery-protocol declares recovery acceptance under criteria weaker than Core §21.5.
tests.expected_result: capability-ownership-map boundary explicitly states composition fails closed if CW recovery declares acceptance under criteria weaker than Core §21.5. Fail closed.
tests.verification: capability-ownership-map capability_boundaries entry for ptr.failure-semantics-and-recovery. ptr-specification-v16.0.0.md §21.9 declares extensions MUST NOT weaken §21.5. creative-writing-bind-template capabilities_extended.does_not_modify includes 'Core §21.5 reconstruction acceptance standard'.

tests.scenario: CW writing-editing-critique-preservation-conversion declares that editing from conversation memory is permitted when a canonical artifact exists.
tests.expected_result: capability-ownership-map boundary explicitly states composition fails closed if CW permits editing from memory when a canonical artifact exists. Fail closed.
tests.verification: capability-ownership-map capability_boundaries entry for editing-discipline.universal. editing-discipline-v16.0.0.md §4 Canonical Source Rule and §11 Bolt-on Extensions rule. creative-writing-bind-template capabilities_extended.does_not_modify includes 'Core §4 canonical source rule'.

notes: Tests verify that the v16 specification structurally enforces fail-closed behavior for each named category. Because CoSyn v16 is interpreted in-chat governance (not an executable runtime), 'verification' means the specification structurally requires the behavior — implementable by a governed process, a validator, or a future runtime. Silent reconciliation would be a specification defect.
All 20 adversarial tests pass structurally. No specification defect detected. No conflict category is silently reconciled by any Core or bolt-on artifact.
The single_ownership_registry in capability-ownership-map.json is the machine-checkable authority-boundary index that composition-time validators use to detect duplicate ownership.
